lines.text: In twenty seventeen, a fundraiser called "I'm afraid of the dark" asked Poland to save a little boy.
Antosh was two and a half, and he had eye cancer.
More than six and a half thousand people gave. Half a million zloty.
The organizer made him up, and spent the money on himself.
One famous donor got a refund. Six and a half thousand others did not.
Poles now give around two billion zloty a year through online fundraisers.
In the US, medical fundraisers on GoFundMe raised over two billion dollars in just five years.
On most platforms, that money takes the same path.
From the donors, through the platform, into the organizer's own account.
After that, all you have is trust.
So we asked: what if the organizer could never touch the money at all?
With Earmark, donations wait in a vault that nobody holds the key to. Not the organizer. Not us.
The clinic confirms the treatment before anyone can give.
When the target is reached, the money goes straight to the clinic.
If it isn't, every donor takes their own money back.
No middleman holding the money. Just rules, written in code, that nobody can bend.
